result:
I graded submission s1 for quiz 0001 and wrote the grades to `grades/0001-s1.json`. You got 2 items correct, 2 partial and 2 wrong.

| Item | Verdict | Why |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | correct | The loop is what makes a system an agent. |
| q2 | wrong | The model doesn't open the booking system. It outputs a request naming the tool and its arguments, and the program runs the tool. |
| q3 | correct | A step limit is the right stopping condition when the agent keeps repeating itself. |
| q4 | wrong | The answer is 4 model calls, not 1. The model never runs the three tools inside one call. The program runs them between calls, and the model is called again after each result. |
| q5 | partial | You said the result goes back to the model, which is right. You left out why: the model needs it to choose its next step or write the final answer. |
| q6 | partial | Right that the model picks a tool from the names and descriptions it is given. Wrong that it remembers earlier sessions on its own. |

q2 and q4 both come from believing the model runs the tools itself (misconception M4). The q6 slip is a second one: the model has no memory of earlier sessions unless the program sends that information again (M3). The grades file has feedback for each item.

I also added learning record `0003-model-does-not-run-tools-or-remember.md` and updated `NOTES.md`. `submissions/s2.json`, your later attempt, is still ungraded.

**Next step:** redraw your laser-cutter request as a timeline with two columns, "model" and "program". Mark every model call and every tool run. You should end up with 4 model calls for the three-tool question. That timeline also sets up the next topic, what the model sees each call and how the assistant can remember a student between visits.

Do you want me to grade s2 next?
